article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Sativa / 40% Indica
Genetics: Trainwreck × Jack Herer
Breeder: Green House Seed Co.
THC Content: 24.65%
CBD Content: 0.26%
CBG Content: 0.60%
Terpene Profile: Alpha-Pinene , D-Limonene , Humulene
Primary Flavors: Pine, Lemon, Earth, Haze, Herbal Spice
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 Weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Mid to Late October
Indoor Yield: Medium to High
Outdoor Yield: 700 g/Plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Dark Phoenix earns its dramatic name through one of the more unusual visual transformations found in modern cannabis cultivation . As flowering progresses, certain plants develop striking blue and nearly black foliage surrounding elongated, resin-covered buds that rise in distinctive foxtail formations. Yet its appearance represents only part of the appeal. Created by Green House Seed Co., this sativa-dominant hybrid combines two legendary American marijuana varieties, Trainwreck and Jack Herer, into a cultivar that balances energetic mental stimulation with comfortable physical relaxation.

The fragrance is equally expressive, bringing together fresh pine, earthy Haze, sharp lemon, and pungent herbal spice. Unlike heavily sedating hybrids developed primarily for evening consumption, this strain offers a more stimulating experience that may complement creative interests and relaxed daytime activities. Its vigorous branching, considerable flowering stretch, and colorful floral development also make it an intriguing option for cultivators seeking genetics with both historical significance and distinctive modern characteristics.
Genetics and Lineage

Dark Phoenix originates from a cross between California Trainwreck and Jack Herer, bringing together two influential genetic lines associated with the development of modern sativa-dominant cannabis. Green House Seed Co. selected these parents to combine Trainwreck’s distinctive floral structure and physical effects with the aromatic complexity and substantial production potential of Jack Herer. The finished hybrid contains approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica genetics, reflecting a balanced breeding approach rather than an attempt to produce an exceptionally narrow-leaved or long-flowering plant. Its growth characteristics reveal contributions from both parents, particularly the vigorous branching, elongated flowers, and substantial trichome production that distinguish mature specimens.

Trainwreck has deep roots in Northern California’s cannabis culture , particularly around Humboldt County, where the cultivar gained recognition during the era of clone-preserved marijuana genetics. Its commonly reported ancestry includes Mexican and Thai sativa genetics combined with Afghani indica, although the exact historical pedigree of the original selection remains uncertain. Trainwreck became influential through its penetrating citrus-pine fragrance, rapid cerebral effects, and unusually shaped flowers.

Jack Herer introduces a different breeding tradition. Originally developed by Sensi Seeds in the Netherlands, the historic Jack Herer line combines Haze , Northern Lights #5, and Shiva Skunk genetics. Haze contributes aromatic complexity and stimulating characteristics, while Northern Lights and Skunk influences provide structural strength, resin production, and a more substantial physical component. By combining these genetic families, Green House Seed Co. created a hybrid that preserves the recognizable qualities of both parents while introducing its own distinctive appearance and effects.
Effects and Experience

The psychoactive experience of Dark Phoenix begins with an uplifting cerebral character that can develop relatively quickly after inhalation. A noticeable shift in mental energy may accompany the onset, making ordinary surroundings feel more engaging and encouraging spontaneous conversation or creative exploration. Rather than producing the overwhelming mental acceleration associated with certain highly stimulating sativas, this cultivar is intended to deliver a more balanced experience. Jack Herer’s influence is particularly apparent in the sense of mental brightness, while Trainwreck contributes an underlying physical calm that helps distinguish the combination from a purely energetic marijuana variety. Music, artistic activities, and informal social settings may become especially enjoyable, although individual responses depend considerably on dosage and tolerance.

Physical relaxation emerges alongside the cerebral effects instead of necessarily arriving as a separate, heavily sedating phase. Muscles may feel less tense, bodily discomfort can become less distracting, and an easygoing sense of comfort may accompany the initial euphoria. Green House Seed Co. describes the cultivar as suitable for daytime consumption because its effects can remain relatively clear-headed and creative. Nevertheless, the reported THC concentration of approximately 24.65% means that significant intoxication is possible even when consumers feel mentally alert. Tasks requiring accurate judgment, coordination, or sustained attention can become more difficult, making driving and other safety-sensitive activities inappropriate after consumption.

Larger amounts may substantially alter the experience. Excessive THC exposure can produce racing thoughts, anxiety, dizziness, dry mouth, irritated eyes, or an uncomfortable increase in heart rate. The stimulating character may intensify these reactions in sensitive individuals, particularly those unfamiliar with potent sativa-dominant weed. Starting with a small amount and assessing its effects carefully is important, since cannabis experiences cannot be predicted reliably from genetic classification alone.
Medical Benefits

Dark Phoenix may interest medical marijuana consumers looking for a combination of subjective mental uplift and physical relaxation. Its Trainwreck ancestry has a longstanding association with medicinal cannabis culture, while Jack Herer contributes a reputation for stimulating and mood-altering effects. Chronic discomfort, muscular tension, and stress-related symptoms are among the reasons some consumers explore THC-containing products. Clinical research has found that certain standardized cannabis preparations may provide modest relief for some forms of chronic pain, particularly neuropathic pain. However, these findings do not establish that individual flower strains will produce equivalent results. No controlled clinical trials have demonstrated that Dark Phoenix itself effectively treats pain, fatigue, depression, or other medical conditions.

Its stimulating properties may seem appealing to individuals experiencing low motivation or daytime fatigue, but high-THC cannabis should not be considered an established treatment for these symptoms. Although temporary euphoria can improve subjective mood, THC may also worsen anxiety, interfere with concentration, and affect sleep quality when used frequently. The breeder reports CBD at approximately 0.26%, indicating that this is predominantly a THC-rich cultivar rather than a balanced cannabinoid preparation. Anyone considering cannabis for ongoing medical symptoms should consult a qualified healthcare professional, particularly when taking prescription medications or managing psychiatric, cardiovascular, or neurological conditions.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The fragrance of Dark Phoenix has a distinctly traditional sativa character, favoring botanical sharpness over the sugary aromas common in contemporary dessert hybrids. Fresh pine dominates the initial impression, suggesting crushed evergreen needles and resinous woodland herbs. Beneath that brightness lies the earthy, slightly woody character associated with classic Haze genetics. Breaking apart the flowers releases another layer of complexity, where lemon zest, pungent spice, and the penetrating herbal aroma of Trainwreck become more noticeable. The combination creates a fragrance that feels exceptionally fresh without losing the deeper, more aggressive qualities expected from potent cannabis.

Green House Seed Co. identifies alpha-pinene, D-limonene, and alpha-humulene as the cultivar’s most prominent terpenes. Alpha-pinene contributes the recognizable evergreen fragrance, while limonene introduces sharper citrus characteristics. Humulene supplies woody, herbal, and slightly bitter notes that reinforce the earthy foundation. These aromatic compounds interact with numerous additional volatile substances, producing a bouquet that cannot be fully explained by three terpenes alone. During consumption, pine and lemon may appear first, followed by peppery spice and a lingering earthy Haze finish. Proper drying and curing help preserve the delicate citrus compounds, while airtight storage protects the aromatic complexity that gives the cultivar its distinctive identity.
Growing Information

Dark Phoenix exhibits vigorous growth that requires more attention to vertical space than its moderate overall size might initially suggest. During vegetative development, the plant establishes strong branches and an increasingly substantial framework. The most significant transformation occurs during the first weeks of flowering, when pronounced stretching causes both the central stem and surrounding branches to gain considerable height. Green House Seed Co. describes a distinctive crown-shaped structure, with vigorous lateral branches rising toward the upper canopy. Indoor growers working with limited headroom may benefit from topping before flowering or applying low-stress training to encourage a wider, more evenly distributed arrangement of branches. Because its stretching can be substantial, canopy management is best considered early rather than after the plant has developed heavy flowers.

Indoor flowering requires approximately 56–70 days, equivalent to eight to ten weeks. Floral development begins energetically, with prominent early flower clusters forming along the branches before gradually connecting into longer colas. As maturity approaches, these structures can develop noticeable foxtailing, where individual clusters of calyxes extend outward into narrow, irregular formations. In this cultivar, foxtailing can be a natural genetic characteristic rather than an automatic indication of excessive heat or light stress. Trichome production becomes increasingly visible across the elongated flowers, giving mature buds a heavily frosted appearance. Another remarkable feature is the potential development of dark pigmentation. Certain phenotypes produce blue, purple, or nearly black foliage during late flowering, although these colors are not guaranteed in every plant.

Indoor yields are classified as medium to high by the breeder, with actual production depending on lighting, root development, environmental control, and cultivation technique. Strong branching can support substantial flower formation, but tall colas may require additional support as their weight increases. Consistent airflow remains important because densely developed floral sections can retain moisture, especially where overlapping branches restrict circulation. Growers should also maintain balanced nutrition throughout flowering rather than assuming vigorous growth requires excessive fertilization. Individual plants may respond differently to feeding strength, irrigation frequency, and training intensity.

Outdoor cultivation favors locations with long, reasonably warm growing seasons extending through October. Under suitable conditions, mature plants can reach approximately 170–200 centimeters tall, with Green House Seed Co. estimating yields around 700 grams per plant. Harvest generally occurs between the middle and end of October in the Northern Hemisphere. This relatively late finishing period requires consideration in climates where autumn rainfall , prolonged humidity, or falling temperatures become problematic. The cultivar’s strong branches provide a useful foundation for developing colas, while its distinctive foliage and elongated flowers can make mature specimens particularly striking. For cultivators who appreciate classic sativa-influenced structure without the exceptionally long flowering cycles of some tropical genetics, Dark Phoenix offers an interesting compromise between vigorous growth and manageable maturation.
FAQ
Is Dark Phoenix an indica or sativa strain?

Dark Phoenix is a sativa-dominant hybrid containing approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica genetics. Its Trainwreck and Jack Herer ancestry contributes uplifting cerebral effects, physical relaxation, vigorous branching, and elongated flowers. The combination offers a balanced experience rather than the heavily sedating character often associated with indica-dominant marijuana.
How strong is Dark Phoenix marijuana?

Green House Seed Co. reports approximately 24.65% THC, 0.26% CBD, and 0.60% CBG. These concentrations indicate substantial psychoactive potency, although laboratory results can vary between individual plants and harvests. Consumers with limited THC tolerance should approach this cultivar cautiously, particularly because its stimulating effects can become intense at higher doses.
What does Dark Phoenix taste like?

Its primary flavors include fresh pine, lemon zest, earthy Haze, woody herbs, and peppery spice. Trainwreck contributes pungent citrus and herbal characteristics, while Jack Herer introduces complex pine and earthy notes. Alpha-pinene, D-limonene, and alpha-humulene are the prominent terpenes identified by the breeder.
Is Dark Phoenix good for daytime use?

The breeder describes Dark Phoenix as a daytime-friendly hybrid because of its uplifting mental effects and relatively balanced physical relaxation. Moderate consumption may feel compatible with undemanding creative or recreational activities. However, its high THC content can impair concentration, coordination, and judgment regardless of whether the consumer feels energetic.
How long does Dark Phoenix take to flower?

Indoor flowering generally requires eight to ten weeks, or approximately 56–70 days. Outdoor plants typically reach harvest maturity from mid to late October in Northern Hemisphere climates. Under favorable conditions, mature outdoor specimens can reach 170–200 centimeters tall and produce approximately 700 grams of dried flower per plant.
Final Thoughts on Dark Phoenix

Dark Phoenix illustrates the enduring value of classic cannabis genetics when combined through thoughtful modern breeding. Trainwreck supplies pungent aromatic intensity, distinctive floral development, and physical relaxation, while Jack Herer contributes the fresh pine character, cerebral stimulation, and productive growth that made it an influential marijuana variety . Together, these parents create a hybrid with a recognizable personality that extends beyond conventional indica and sativa descriptions.

Its dramatic foxtailing, potential for nearly black foliage, and substantial resin production add considerable visual appeal, while the lemon-pine fragrance provides a refreshing alternative to dessert-dominated cannabis genetics. Growers must account for vigorous flowering stretch and a relatively late outdoor harvest, but strong branching and medium-to-high production potential offer meaningful rewards. For enthusiasts interested in the intersection of Northern California cannabis heritage and Dutch breeding traditions, Dark Phoenix remains a distinctive sativa-dominant hybrid with both historical depth and contemporary appeal.
